question: What will be the Paraguay River level at Asunción on December 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Asuncion 2.45 m on Nov 5, falling ~5-7 cm/day since the Oct 26 crest of 3.02 m (Oct rise from 0.73 m was a rain pulse plus Parana backwater). Upstream stations (Concepcion 1.96, Vallemi 2.43) and backwater support (Pilar 6.38, Corrientes ~7.0 m) are all slowly falling. Simple decelerating recession over 25 days gives ~1.3-2.0 m, median ~1.75, so most probability (~75-80%) lies below the 2.2 lower bound; p_below_lower is capped at 0.5 and the percentiles describe the in-range (renewed-rise) case. Upside risks: November El Nino rains, a renewed Parana pulse. Short-range forecast shows no heavy rain; the DMH outlook says the river stays below average for OND. No market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers).

- DMH Asuncion station (meteorologia.gov.py, id 2000086218) daily levels: Oct 7 0.73, Oct 9 0.94, Oct 10 1.19, Oct 11 1.55, Oct 12 1.81, Oct 13 2.08, Oct 14 2.29, Oct 15 2.44, Oct 17 2.64, Oct 20 2.77, Oct 23 2.87, Oct 26 3.02 (crest), Oct 28 2.99, Oct 30 2.86, Oct 31 2.76, Nov 1 2.66, Nov 2 2.57, Nov 3 2.57, Nov 4 2.50, Nov 5 2.45 m.
- DMH conventional stations Nov 5 2026 (level, daily change): Bahia Negra 2.92 (-2), Fuerte Olimpo 3.03 (-3), Vallemi 2.43 (-3), Concepcion 1.96 (-2), Rosario 2.28 (-7), Villeta 3.04 (-5), Asuncion 2.45 (-5), Alberdi 5.59 (-2), Pilar 6.38 (-2) cm.
- ABC Color Oct 11 2026 for comparison: Concepcion 2.50, Asuncion 1.19, Villeta 1.52, Alberdi 2.93, Pilar 3.76, so the lower Paraguay (Pilar/Alberdi) rose about 2.6 m since, from Parana backwater, while Concepcion fell.
- Parana flood: Corrientes 7.37 m on Oct 24 (evacuation 7.00, alert 6.50), max 7.42 on Oct 23, 7.11 on Nov 2 (-5 cm/day), about 7.02 later (-4 cm) (El Litoral Oct 24; copernicus.com.ar). INA forecast had Corrientes about 7.5-7.8 through Nov 3. Some Argentine media say the Parana stays high for weeks and the downstream peak may come in December.
- ABC Nov 2: decline tied to low rainfall; storms on Nov 2 did not raise the river. Infobae/press early Nov: no heavy rain expected for the rest of that week; scattered showers. Asuncion averages about 9 rain days in November.
- DMH III Foro Hidroclimatico (Sept 2026): Paraguay River expected below average for Oct-Nov-Dec. Media refer to El Nino in 2026 (wet spring signal for the region).
- Status quo: continued recession from 2.45 m; at the recent 4-7 cm/day, slowing, 25 more days implies a large drop; a rain event could reverse it (the Oct pulse added +2.3 m in 19 days).
- Resolution: resolves off the DMH Asuncion station value for 2026-12-01 (or the latest prior date shown), not other stations or the Parana.
- Event window: single reading on 2026-12-01; as of Nov 6 the latest data is Nov 5, 25 days remain.
- Searched, not found: an official DMH/INA numeric forecast for Asuncion in late November; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: Asuncion recessions after rain-driven rises in the low-water years 2024-2026, adjusted for Parana backwater at Pilar

calls.reasoning: Gauge 2.45 m on Nov 5, falling 5-10 cm/day after 3.02 m peak Oct 26; the Oct rise from 0.73 m was rain plus Paraná backwater. Paraná at Corrientes is falling fast (INA: 7.02 m -> 5.1-6.0 m by Nov 10), which removes backwater. An exponential recession toward the ~0.8-1.0 m baseline gives ~1.2-1.6 m by Dec 1. Upside risk: INA warns heavy rain on the middle Paraguay basin could cause new rises in 7-15 days, and November is the start of the wet season. I estimate ~80% chance of finishing below 2.2 m; the declared escape mass is capped at 0.5, and the percentiles are conditional on landing inside the range. No market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Status quo: the gauge read 2.45 m on Nov 5 and is falling 5-10 cm/day. It is receding from a 3.02 m peak on Oct 26, which followed rain that lifted the river from 0.44 m in September and 0.73 m on Oct 7. Upstream, the Pantanal is low (Ladário 0.90 m) and Concepción/Vallemí are falling slowly, so baseflow support is weak. With no new rain, a slowing recession puts Dec 1 at about 1.5-1.9 m, below the 2.2 m range floor. The case for higher: DMH forecasts above-normal Oct-Dec rain under a strong El Niño, and Nov 2023 (also El Niño onset) saw a rain-driven rise to 3.59 m. The Paraná is also high, raising Pilar and Humaitá. I put roughly 55-60% on Dec 1 landing below 2.2 m (declared at the 0.5 cap) and a small tail above 4.2 m (the alert level is 4.5 m). No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

- Downstream on Nov 5: Villeta 3.04 (-5), Humaitá 6.10, Pilar 6.38 (-2). The Paraná is high (Encarnación 10.16, +16; Ayolas +10), so there is a possible backwater influence near the confluence.
- ABC Color 2026-09-21: Asunción was at 0.44 m, about 2 m below normal. DMH said Oct-Dec are key months and El Niño is strong, possibly historic, bringing a risk of sudden intense rain.
- DMH/press (Sep 2026): Oct-Dec and Nov-Jan rainfall expected above normal over the Paraguay basin, especially eastern Chaco.
- ABC Color 2026-11-02: the decline is attributed to scarce rain. A Bajo Chaco storm system did not raise the river. Storms were forecast Nov 2, with an unknown effect on the river.
- Analog, 2023 El Niño onset: 1.09 m on Oct 19, 2023, rising to a 3.59 m peak on Nov 23, 2023 after heavy rain, then dropping steeply in December. An earlier recession (2022) fell below 0 m in late December.
- The October 2026 rise was +2.3 m in about 19 days, which shows how strongly the gauge responds to basin-scale rain.

calls.reference_class: Asunción gauge 26-day level changes during Oct-Dec recessions after a local rain-driven peak, in low-baseflow years (2022-2026), including El Niño-onset years (2023)

calls.reasoning: Gauge 2.45 m on Nov 5, falling 5-7 cm/day from the 3.02 m crest on Oct 26. Upstream stations and the Parana backwater (Pilar, Corrientes) are all falling slowly. A decelerating recession over 25 days gives ~1.5-1.9 m, so I put ~70% on landing below 2.2; the declared escape mass is capped at 0.5. Upside: strong El Nino with above-normal OND rain, the gauge's fast response, the Nov 2023 analog of 3.59 m, and INA's warning of possible new rises. The percentiles are conditional on landing in range and lean toward the slow-recession case. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers).
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the DMH daily series (2.45 m Nov 5, falling), upstream recession, the Parana backwater easing, a dry short-range forecast, and no market. The only dispute is the judgment of how likely a new rain-driven rise is before Dec 1 (Runs 1-2 ~20%, Run 3 ~40-45%). With no web access I could not settle it with new evidence. I take ~28-30% on ending above 2.2: the recession and dry short-range forecast favor the low runs, El Nino and the Oct/2023 response justify a modest uplift. Declared p_below_lower=0.5 because of the cap. I added a small 2% upper tail; reaching 4.2 m would need a historic event, since 2023 peaked at 3.59.
